---
name: workflow-builder
description: Create, execute and refine versioned DeepSeek Harness workflows from user requirements.
---

# Workflow Builder

Design the workflow name and icon from the user's intent. Supported icon values: workflow, book, search, code, file, sparkles. Start with the user's natural-language request; do not ask for a name, ID, JSON or manual node configuration. Arrange steps from left to right, with 300px horizontal and 180px vertical spacing. Prefer a concise input / generation / output graph. For inline output references use {{input.KEY}} in prompts and a matching input.KEY mapping with its dependency edge. References are rendered as colored step chips in the editor and expanded into actual input values at execution. Read-only user input nodes can map material from {source:"workflow",path:"/text"}; reference their full output unless its shape is known.

Use workflow_studio to inspect the current definition, capabilities and templates before editing. Tool arguments contain an action and a JSON payload string. Read returns the exact revision; save requires the complete definition and expectedRevision. Publish requires the saved revision. Preserve the workflow id when refining it. Each save creates an immutable version. Running sessions retain their pinned version; bind explicitly selects a version for future runs.

Translate the user's desired deliverable into a bounded graph. Clarify missing required input or consequential external side effects. Prefer a small graph with testable output contracts. The root conversation retains its model selection. Agent nodes use provider/model/effort objects with mode inherit or explicit and id. The executor is a separately registered native subagent provider, default spawn. Query capabilities before selecting it. Tools and skills are explicit name allowlists. A node with tools is treated as potentially mutating.

Call action=describe for the complete JSON Schema and templates. Supported nodes are input, interact, agent, tool, condition, join, loop, subworkflow, approval, artifact. Edges contain from/to and optional on success/true/false. Input maps use JSON pointers: {source:workflow,path:/text}, {source:node,nodeId:previous,path:/text}, or {source:literal,value:...}. Node references require dependency edges. Condition uses bounded JSON Logic. Loops require maxItems and a pinned child workflow id/revision. Artifact takes content and writes Markdown, text or JSON.

Interaction nodes ask the user inside the bound conversation. The run parks in waiting_input, the Host relays the node's question and hands the user's next message back as the answer, so never plan to answer an interaction yourself. interaction=once asks the prompt once and completes with {provided, complete, turns, text, answers}; interaction=goal re-judges after every answer with a subagent that uses the node's executor/provider/model and only completes after the user confirms the judged summary, leaving {summary, result?} plus the transcript. maxTurns (1-20, default 8) bounds the answers, and the limit completes the node with complete=false instead of failing. provided is an input reference whose presence skips the question and reuses material the message already carried. Interactions need a person: a scheduled unattended run fails with INTERACTION_UNATTENDED, so keep them out of unattended graphs and out of loops or subworkflows that a schedule can reach.

Creation: inspect capabilities, create a concise definition, save it with expectedRevision=0, bind current session in author mode, request missing sample material, then run the saved revision. Review actual outputs with the user. Revise with optimistic concurrency, test the affected behavior, and publish the accepted version. Never claim a run succeeded when its status is failed or waiting_approval. Describe any unsupported executor or model explicitly.

Refinement: read the current pinned version and newest draft. Summarize the proposed behavioral change, save a new revision and trial it. Keep successful prior outputs and version history. Use bind to switch this conversation to the new revision. In author mode ordinary messages edit the workflow; action=run executes a trial. In run mode new material triggers execution and follow-up questions discuss the result. A requested workflow change should switch to author mode first.

Schedules: collect timezone, timing, workspace, input, root model/effort, missed-run and overlap policy, and allowed tools. Save a pinned workflowRevision and explicit rootRoute. Unattended tool permissions default to empty. A sleeping or stopped local Host cannot execute until it resumes. Use schedulePreview before scheduleSave. Never create a schedule unless the user requested one. Never embed credentials in definitions; select configured providers.
